doc.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023

title: Jack Sheldon, The Creeper, and contractor Bobby Helfer
summary: Story of Jack Sheldon arriving late to a Universal double session, claiming he was fogged in, and slipping out at the end.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Did you sit next to Jack Sheldon on occasion?

Oh yeah, oh yeah I sure did. I’ve got a couple of stories about that too, I don’t know — well yeah, I could tell you, I could tell you, beautiful. We were at Universal, we had a nine in the morning call and there was a double session and it was a Monday. And we called him “The Creeper.” Jack was The Creeper. And the reason he was called The Creeper was cause he’d creep in and then he’d creep out. And so we’re doing this nine in the morning double session at Universal and the contractor’s name was Bobby Helfer. And Bobby was a real, real, I mean he was absolutely fantastic as a contractor as far as if we went 30 seconds over we got overtime, we got 20 minutes overtime. I mean he did not give in at all. He was really a wonderful contractor for musicians. But he was also very — he didn’t want anybody to — he wouldn’t go to lunch with anybody or anything like that because he thought they were kissing ass and they would want work from him. So anyhow so he’s the contractor at Universal. Now Jack’s on the call. Everybody’s there, and like I said it wasn’t an hour before, we’d get there ten minutes, five minutes before the session, get out our horns and get ready to perform. And no Jack. Jack’s not there. So nine o’clock goes by, ten after nine, twenty after, no Jack. Well somebody mentioned that Jack was in San Francisco that weekend, he was doing a gig in San Francisco. So Jack comes in and as he’s walking in Bobby Helfer immediately goes up to him as he’s walking in to come to his chair and he says to him, he says, before he could say anything he says, “I got fogged in, Bobby.” And Bobby said, “I called. There was no fog, and there was no reason —” And Jack Sheldon says, “Bobby,” he says, “there are many ways to get fogged in.” That was Jack’s line. And Jack came and sat down next to me and we did the session and everything was beautiful. Jack was wonderful. And at the end of the double date, so 9-12 and 1-4, at 4:00 I’m putting — I’m pretty quick because I had another session to go to and I’m putting my horns away. I turned and Jack’s gone. The Creeper was gone. So he would creep in and creep out and but his personality was so beautiful and he was so funny and just a sweetheart of a man and so natural.
